title: Create a Client-Ready Marketing Strategy Deck
learning_outcomes: Conduct a structured business audit using free competitive intelligence tools
Define measurable goals and target personas for a marketing strategy
Plan a channel mix with budget allocation justified by data
Create a 90-day tactical execution calendar with specific actions
Design a professional pitch deck that could be presented to a real client

steps.title: Conduct Business Audit and Competitor Analysis
steps.instructions:
1. Choose a business to create a strategy for. Options:
   - A real local business in your city (restaurant, salon, tuition centre, gym)
   - A hypothetical D2C brand: 'SpiceCraft' — an online store selling premium Indian spice blends from Bhopal, targeting home cooks aged 25-45 in metro cities
2. Audit the chosen business's current digital presence:
   - Website: Visit their site. Note: design quality, mobile-friendliness, page speed (test at pagespeed.web.dev), CTAs, content quality
   - Social Media: Check Instagram, Facebook, YouTube. Note: follower count, posting frequency, engagement rate (likes+comments/followers x 100)
   - Google Business: Search for them on Google Maps. Note: rating, review count, photos, completeness
   - SEO: Search their main keywords on Google. Where do they rank? Page 1? Not at all?
3. Identify 3 competitors and analyze them:
   - Go to SimilarWeb.com > enter each competitor's website
   - Note: monthly visits, traffic sources, top countries, bounce rate
   - Go to Meta Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library) > search competitor names
   - Note: Are they running ads? What type? What messaging?
   - Check their social media: What content works best? (sort by most liked)
4. Open Google Trends (trends.google.com):
   - Search the business's main keywords
   - Set location to India, last 12 months
   - Note: Is demand growing or declining? Any seasonal patterns?
5. Create a summary document with:
   - Business current state (score 1-10 for: Website, SEO, Social, Ads, Email)
   - Competitor comparison table (Business vs Comp 1 vs Comp 2 vs Comp 3)
   - SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats)
   - Top 3 gaps/opportunities identified
6. Take screenshots of all research (SimilarWeb, Meta Ad Library, Google Trends).
7. Save this research — you will use it in the next steps.

steps.title: Define Goals, KPIs, and Target Personas
steps.instructions:
1. Based on your audit, define 3-5 SMART goals for the next 6 months:
   Goal template: '[Action verb] [specific metric] from [current] to [target] by [date]'
   Example goals for SpiceCraft:
   - Increase monthly website visitors from 500 to 5,000 by December 2026
   - Generate 200 email subscribers per month by October 2026
   - Achieve Rs 3,00,000 monthly online revenue by March 2027
   - Grow Instagram followers from 200 to 5,000 by December 2026
   - Reduce customer acquisition cost from Rs 800 to Rs 300 by January 2027
2. For each goal, define the KPI and measurement method:
   | Goal | KPI | How to Measure | Tool |
   Create this table in your document.
3. Create 2 detailed buyer personas:
   Persona 1 template:
   - Name: (e.g., 'Cooking Priya')
   - Age: (e.g., 28-35)
   - Location: (e.g., Mumbai, Pune)
   - Occupation: (e.g., IT professional, works from home)
   - Income: (e.g., Rs 8-15 LPA household)
   - Pain Points: (e.g., 'Wants authentic spices but local market quality is inconsistent')
   - Online Behavior: (e.g., 'Watches cooking reels on Instagram, follows food bloggers, orders groceries on BigBasket')
   - Where to reach them: (e.g., 'Instagram Reels, YouTube cooking channels, food Facebook groups')
   - What would make them buy: (e.g., 'Recipe video showing the spice in action + first-order discount')
4. Create Persona 2 following the same template but for a different segment.
5. Map the customer journey for Persona 1:
   - Awareness: How do they first discover the brand?
   - Consideration: What makes them consider buying?
   - Decision: What pushes them to purchase?
   - Retention: What brings them back?
   - Referral: What makes them tell friends?
6. Document everything clearly — this will go into your pitch deck.

steps.title: Plan Channel Mix and Budget Allocation
steps.instructions:
1. Based on your personas and goals, select marketing channels. For each channel, justify WHY:
   - Where does your persona spend time? (Channel selection)
   - What's the estimated CAC per channel? (Efficiency)
   - What's the timeline to results? (Quick wins vs long-term)
2. Open Google Sheets and create a Budget Allocation spreadsheet.
3. Set total monthly budget: Rs 41,667 (which is Rs 5 Lakh annual / 12 months).
4. Allocate budget across channels. Example for SpiceCraft (Growth stage):
   | Channel | % | Monthly (Rs) | Justification |
   | SEO & Content | 20% | 8,333 | Blog recipes drive organic traffic, compounds over time |
   | Instagram Ads | 25% | 10,417 | Persona is active on Instagram, visual product |
   | Google Ads | 20% | 8,333 | Capture search intent for 'buy spices online' |
   | Influencer (Food bloggers) | 15% | 6,250 | Trust factor, UGC content, authentic reviews |
   | Email Marketing | 10% | 4,167 | Nurture subscribers, repeat purchases |
   | Tools & Software | 10% | 4,167 | Canva, MailerLite, analytics tools |
5. For each channel, estimate expected results:
   - Instagram Ads: Rs 10,417 spend, CPM Rs 150, estimated reach: 69,000, CTR 2%, clicks: 1,380, conversion 3%, orders: 41
   - Show the math: Expected revenue = 41 orders x Rs 500 AOV = Rs 20,500. ROAS = 2.0x
6. Create a quarterly view: How will budget shift from Q1 to Q2?
   - Q1: More on awareness (ads, content)
   - Q2: Shift towards conversion (retargeting, email)
7. Add a 'What If' section: If budget doubles, where would extra money go and why?
8. Save this spreadsheet — link it in your deck.

steps.title: Build 90-Day Tactical Execution Calendar
steps.instructions:
1. Create a new sheet in your Google Spreadsheet called '90-Day Plan'.
2. Structure it as a weekly calendar with columns: Week | Channel | Tasks | Deliverables | Owner | Status
3. Month 1 (Weeks 1-4) — Foundation & Quick Wins:
   Week 1:
   - Set up GA4 + GTM on website
   - Create Instagram Business account, optimize bio
   - Set up MailerLite account, create welcome sequence
   - Research top 20 keywords for SEO
   Week 2:
   - Launch first Google Ads campaign (brand keywords)
   - Create first 7 Instagram posts (batch create in Canva)
   - Write 2 blog posts targeting long-tail keywords
   - Set up email opt-in form on website
   Week 3:
   - Launch Instagram Ads (first campaign, test 3 creatives)
   - Reach out to 5 micro-influencers (food bloggers)
   - Publish blog posts, share on social
   - Send first email newsletter
   Week 4:
   - Review all Week 1-3 data, identify winners
   - Scale winning ad creative, pause losers
   - Confirm 1-2 influencer collaborations
   - Create content for next month
4. Month 2 (Weeks 5-8) — Scale & Optimize:
   Fill in similar detail for each week. Focus on: scaling winners, adding retargeting, more content, first influencer posts going live.
5. Month 3 (Weeks 9-12) — Review & Expand:
   Focus on: performance review, new channels, loyalty program, referral campaign, reporting.
6. Create a separate Content Calendar for Month 1:
   - Day-by-day Instagram posting plan (Mon-Sat)
   - Include: post type (Reel/Carousel/Story), topic, caption hook, hashtags
   - At least 20 content pieces planned
7. Save and format the calendar clearly. This will be referenced in your deck.

steps.title: Design 10-Slide Pitch Deck in Gamma or Canva
steps.instructions:
1. Go to gamma.app (sign up free) OR use Canva Presentations.
2. If using Gamma: Click 'Create' > 'Presentation' > Enter your topic: 'Digital Marketing Strategy for [Business Name] — 6 Month Growth Plan'. Let AI generate a base, then customize heavily.
   If using Canva: Search for 'Marketing Proposal' templates and pick a professional one.
3. Create exactly 10 slides with this structure:

   Slide 1 — Cover:
   - Title: 'Digital Marketing Strategy Proposal'
   - Subtitle: Business name
   - Your name, TechPath Academy, Date
   - Clean, professional design

   Slide 2 — About Us:
   - Brief intro (who you are, credentials)
   - Key stats: '6-month intensive training', 'Google & Meta certified', '10+ live projects'

   Slide 3 — The Challenge:
   - Current problems identified in audit
   - Use specific numbers from your research
   - Visual: before screenshot or current metrics

   Slide 4 — Market Opportunity:
   - Industry data (market size, growth rate)
   - Google Trends screenshot showing demand
   - Competitor gaps you identified

   Slide 5 — Our Strategy:
   - High-level approach (3-4 key pillars)
   - Visual: simple diagram showing the strategy
   - Channels selected and why

   Slide 6 — Tactical Plan:
   - 90-day overview (Month 1, 2, 3 key actions)
   - Timeline visual
   - Content strategy summary

   Slide 7 — Expected Results:
   - Projected KPIs at 3, 6, 12 months
   - Traffic, leads, revenue projections (use your earlier calculations)
   - Comparison: current vs projected

   Slide 8 — Case Study/Social Proof:
   - If you have a previous project result, show it
   - If not, show a relevant industry case study with attribution
   - Before/after format with numbers

   Slide 9 — Investment:
   - Pricing (your fees + ad budget)
   - What's included in each package
   - ROI justification: 'For every Rs 1 invested, expect Rs 3-5 return within 6 months'

   Slide 10 — Next Steps:
   - Clear CTA: 'Let's schedule a 30-minute discovery call'
   - Timeline: Onboarding (Week 1) > Strategy (Week 2) > Execution (Week 3+)
   - Contact details

4. Design tips:
   - Use consistent colors (max 3)
   - One idea per slide
   - More visuals, less text
   - Use charts/icons instead of bullet points where possible
   - Ensure text is readable (min 18pt for body)
5. Export as PDF and also keep the editable link.
6. Practice presenting: Read through all 10 slides aloud. Time yourself — aim for 8-10 minutes total.
7. Take a screenshot of your complete deck (all slides in grid view).
8. Peer review: Share with 1 classmate and get feedback on clarity and professionalism.
